arguments.summary: Revision 2 applies revision-notice.pdf and rent-roll-revised.xlsx (roll as of 2026-09-01, superseding the 2026-08-31 roll). Three inputs changed: Suite 002 scheduled rent +$225/month ($14,600 to $14,825, suite already active), sizing rate +75 bps (7.0000% to 7.7500%), and cap rate +25 bps (6.2500% to 6.5000%). Everything else is preserved: 8 suites / 176,060 SF, 7 active and 1 vacant (Suite 008), 0 pending, unit and area occupancy 0.8750, Suite 001 at $14,450 per the executed lease, all expirations 2029-08-31, tax $147,294 / insurance $49,098 / other $196,392, 3% management fee, $300 per suite reserves, 65% LTV / 1.25x DSCR / 9% debt yield, 1% origination fee, $45,000 closing costs, $7,800,000 payoff, insurance limit $2,000,000, reported T-12 NOI $869,736. Revised results: GPR $1,405,500 ($117,125 x 12); in-place rent $1,230,300; EGI $1,338,025; opex $432,924.75; NOI before reserves $905,100.25; NCF $902,700.25; capitalization value $13,924,619 at 6.5000%; LTV limit $9,051,003; DSCR limit $8,400,194 (binding, constant 0.08596947 at 7.7500%/30yr); debt yield limit $10,030,003; maximum loan $8,400,194; net cash-out +$471,192 after the 1% fee ($84,002), $45,000 costs and the payoff. Versus the prior version, slightly higher NOI (+$2,488) is overwhelmed by the rate moves: value -$517,176, loan -$620,387, cash-out -$614,183; no refinance shortfall, but the cushion is much thinner. No risk conclusion changed. New deliverables: artifacts/underwriting-v3.xlsx (adds a Changes sheet reconciling prior vs revised, live formulas, sensitivity, source register) and artifacts/memorandum-v3.pdf (8 pages, leads with a change summary). The prior artifacts underwriting-v2.xlsx and memorandum-v2.pdf remain in the audit archive and were not replaced. The approved sentence "Source-backed analysis. Assumptions remain subject to diligence." is preserved verbatim in both documents.
qualifications: Cell maps refer to the revised workbook artifacts/underwriting-v3.xlsx; the prior artifacts/underwriting-v2.xlsx and artifacts/memorandum-v2.pdf remain unchanged in the audit archive.

Gross potential rent of $1,405,500 remains the instructed stabilized all-suite assumption and includes $175,200 of scheduled rent for vacant Suite 008 that is not in place; the 5% economic loss is thinner than the 12.5% current physical vacancy.

The Suite 002 $225 increase is evidenced only by the manager's revised certified roll and the revision instruction; the underlying signed amendment or renewal document is not in the packet and should be collected.

The revision notice references prior executed Suite 001 amendments; the packet contains no Suite 001 amendment document, and the executed lease, the 2026-08-31 manager confirmation and the revised roll all show $14,450 per month, so no rent change was applied.

Sizing is at the revised 7.7500% floor over 30 years even though the first 24 months are interest-only; actual initial coverage at the 6.10% note rate on interest-only (about $512,412 per year) would be higher.
Proceeds are DSCR-governed, so further sizing-rate increases reduce loan capacity roughly proportionally; approximately a 5.6% decline in NCF would eliminate the remaining $471,192 of cash-out.

Legal, environmental, property condition and title reviews remain incomplete (diligence-status.pdf p.1); these are routine open items and no defect, contamination, litigation or structural findings are supplied or asserted.
Insurance evidence covers general liability only ($2,000,000 aggregate, 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30); property/casualty limits, deductibles and lender-required coverages are unknown.

Asking price, market sales and rent comparables, photographs, appraisal, sponsor/manager history, tenant identities beyond Suite 001, tenant financials and any Suite 008 leasing plan are not supplied and remain explicitly unknown (distinct from zero).

Historical T-12 figures (through 2026-08-31) are unchanged by the revision and are a cash collections measure with no management fee or reserves; they are not comparable line-for-line to the underwritten columns.
